reason: I want to make supporting material, so starting with the collagen instructions and protein machinery seems useful.
expectation: I expect the machinery to use the copied instructions toward making collagen, though amino acids may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The repair signals may help skin cells rebuild the surface, but the current goal focuses on supporting material.

effect: The copied instructions direct the protein machinery to make collagen, so amino acids appear to be the next ingredient.
reaction: The connection to the muscle cells' protein machinery is useful.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, so adding them should advance the supporting material goal.
expectation: I expect the directed builders to assemble a collagen protein, perhaps needing further processing before it can support the tissue.

alternatives.reason: The signals may help rebuild the surface, but I want to finish the collagen path first.

effect: The amino acids formed collagen chains, which now need processing and export to contribute to the damaged site.
reaction: It is useful to see instructions, materials and energy distinguished as separate needs.
reason: Processing and export membranes seem like the next step toward making supporting material available outside the cells.
expectation: I expect the collagen chains to be processed and exported, though I am unsure what form the resulting material will take.

alternatives.reason: The signals may advance surface repair, but I want to continue the collagen path first.

effect: The collagen has been processed and exported into supporting fibers that can contribute to the damaged site.
reaction: It is interesting that cells make material that supports tissue outside them.
reason: Adding the new fibers to the body seems like the direct way to provide support at the scrape.
expectation: I expect the fibers to help rebuild support at the damaged site, though the surface may still need repair.

alternatives.reason: The signals may start surface repair, but I want to finish placing the supporting fibers first.

effect: The supporting fibers have been laid down, and the next goal is to restore the surface.
reaction: The distinction between a temporary seal and rebuilt tissue is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the signals seem relevant to restoring the skin surface.
expectation: I expect the signals to prompt skin cells at the edge to help cover the scrape.

effect: The signals influence edge cells to move and multiply, providing living coverage using materials and energy.
reaction: The distinction between a signal and the cells doing the repair is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should put the spreading cells over the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the cells to restore surface coverage, though the tissue may continue to reorganize afterward.

effect: The surface barrier is restored, while deeper rebuilding and strengthening continue and a scar may remain.
reaction: The ending ties the cellular work back to the same body in a satisfying way.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the supporting fibers was most worthwhile because it connected protein production inside cells to tissue support outside them.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final placement of the spreading cells was predictable because it was the only offered combination, though it completed the repair.

surprise.text: I was interested that collagen needs processing outside the cells before supporting fibers form.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the combinations followed the stated repair goals, although the menu supplied the compatible partners.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter explored a different body process; the connections between cellular work and tissue repair held my interest, though the last steps were predictable.
